title: Cascade Health QBR + Renewal Playbook (draft)
content:
Cascade Health — QBR + Renewal Playbook (draft)

Purpose / meeting objective:
- Run a focused QBR that highlights value delivered in the contract year, surface outstanding risks ahead of renewal (target: 2026-06-30), and propose a renewal structure that balances cost predictability with their peak-agent needs.
- Primary outcomes we want: verbal commitment to a renewal conversation in May, alignment on SLA & capacity proof points, and a follow-up technical deep-dive for dedicated-capacity sizing.

One-line narrative:
- "Redwood has steadily reduced token cost and cut median inference latency for Cascade's clinician-assistant flows by ~30% while enabling secure private deployments; for renewal we shift conversation from feature parity to predictable economics and a staged Dedicated rollout to lock in performance and SLAs."

Account context (brief):
- Use case: clinical knowledge retrieval + assistant for care coordinators (high sensitivity).
- Deployed: Private deployment (VPC) + hosted API fallback for burst traffic.
- Annual ARR: ~$350k (current contract); renewal target volume +20% vs current.
- Key contacts: Daniel Kim (CTO / exec sponsor), Allison Rivera (Dir. Data Science / PO), Priya Shah (Head of IT / security), Omar Li (SRE lead).
- Known concerns: predictable latency during weekday peak (09:00–12:00 PST), cost spikes during monthly batch indexing, SOC2 evidence & audit log retention window.

Slide-by-slide plan (13–20 minutes + Q/A):
1) Title + Agenda (30s): quick wins frame and renewal ask timing.
2) Executive snapshot (1 min): ARR contribution vs ROI statement — "Care coordinator time saved / case throughput" headline with a single chart (monthly savings estimate).
3) Adoption & usage trends (2 min): DAU/MAU of assistant, top intent buckets, pct of requests served by private cluster vs hosted fallback. Key datapoints: 40% reduction in avg task time; 25% of sessions used embeddings-based retrieval.
4) Performance & reliability (2 min): latency P50/P95 trend (last 6 months), incident summary (1 P1 in Sept -> resolved code + infra fix JIRA:CS-842), current SLO attainment. Talking points: root cause, mitigation, longer-term fix (kernel selection tuning rollout).
5) Cost & efficiency (2 min): per-token unit cost trend, effect of KV caching and batching recommendations we applied last quarter (show before/after). Proposed lever: staged quantization + dedup caching to save ~12–15% token cost.
6) Security / compliance & audit readiness (1 min): confirm audit artifacts we can provide (KMS logs, audit retention extension options). Ask: confirm SOC2 timeline from their side.
7) Product roadmap alignment (2 min): upcoming features relevant to Cascade (priority routing for clinicians, improved prefix caching for long contexts). Call out which are GA vs experimental.
8) Renewal proposal & options (3 min): present 3-tier renewal structure (concise table):
   - Option A (Conservative): 12m renewal, hosted + private baseline, 0% uplift, standard SLA
   - Option B (Recommended): 12m renewal, Dedicated pilot (3 months), fixed committed capacity + burst pool, 7% uplift, 99.9% latency SLA for pinned routes
   - Option C (Aggressive): 24m commit, capacity discounts, deeper integration support (onboarding services)
   Talking points: emphasize pilot reduces risk; we can do a canary week to measure tail latency on their worst-case intents.
9) Risk matrix & mitigations (1.5 min): list top risks (exec sponsor churn, budget reprioritization, performance regressions) with concrete mitigations (customer success exec shadow, hold pricing for 60 days pending dedicated pilot results, technical deep-dive + perf acceptance criteria).
10) Asks & next steps (1 min): schedule technical sizing session (by Apr 15), exec renewal review (by May 10), decision target: Jun 15.
11) Appendix & Q/A (remaining time): Link to detailed perf reports, cost model spreadsheet, SSO/KMS checklist.

Tailored talking points / scripting (short bullets to read live):
- To Daniel (CTO): "We want to make the economics predictable for the teams you manage — the dedicated pilot is intentionally limited duration so you can validate latency and cost without a full switch-over."
- To Allison (Dir DS): "We validated that the embedding retention and prefix caching decreased retrieval latency on your top 3 intents — we'll show the per-intent numbers in the appendix."
- To Priya (Head IT): "For audits, we can extend log retention and provide a packaged evidence bundle within 4 weeks of request; we proposed KMS key rotation notes in the security doc."
- For SRE/Infra (Omar): "We will run a shadow workload with pinned routing to catch perf cliffs and validate our kernel selection heuristics before any capacity commit."

Renewal timeline (milestones):
- Mar 20: send pre-read + perf appendix (action: Maya)
- Apr 1–15: technical sizing + Dedicated pilot plan (action: Eng + CS + Customer SRE)
- Apr 20: pilot kick-off (1 week smoke + 2 weeks measurement)
- May 5: internal pricing sign-off (biz ops)
- May 10: exec renewal review meeting with Daniel
- Jun 15: target renewal signature

Risks & mitigations (short):
- Risk: budget reprioritization leads to delay — Mitigation: Offer time-limited pricing hold and 90-day runway for onboarding credits.
- Risk: performance regression under heavy peaked load — Mitigation: run a 3-week dedicated pilot with SLO checks and a rollback policy; include a canary route for clinician-critical intents.
- Risk: compliance evidence gaps for upcoming audit — Mitigation: provide pre-packaged evidence bundle + one week of white-glove support during audit window.

Success metrics & evidence to prepare (we need these slides/data ready in pre-read):
- Usage: monthly active users, session completion rates, % reduction in manual triage time (customer-reported).
- Perf: P50/P95 latency for top 10 intents (past 6 months), error rates, fallback frequency to hosted API.
- Economics: per-token cost trend, unit cost after caching + recommended quantization, estimated Q3 savings by moving X% traffic to Dedicated.
- Reliability: incidents timeline, mean time to recovery, current SLO attainment.

Pre-meeting checklist (CS owner: Maya):
- Export perf charts + one-pager summary (done by Eng: Alex)
- Updated cost model with dedicated pilot assumptions (finance ops: Samir)
- Pre-read + slide deck v0 to customer by Mar 20 (include appendix)
- Confirm exec attendee list & logistics (Allison to confirm)

Open questions / notes to resolve before pre-read:
- Exact renewal date window from legal (ask legal to confirm earliest renewal window).
- Final pilot acceptance criteria (need to define P95 threshold and error budget for pilot).
- Audit log retention desired by Cascade (Priya to confirm).

Action items (owner — due):
- Maya: finalize deck + send pre-read (2026-03-20)
- Alex Torres (Eng): attach perf export & incident postmortem summary (2026-03-18)
- Samir Rao (Finance Ops): update cost model for pilot and three renewal options (2026-03-24)
- Priya Shah (Customer): confirm audit retention requirement (ASAP)

Notes to self / rough brainstorm (informal):
- Consider offering a short-term credits package tied to monthly active users to smooth the renewal conversation.
- Would a month-by-month ramp (commit 6 months then review) be easier politically? Pros: low exec hurdle. Cons: less price certainty.
- Check slack thread #cs-cascade-renewal for any last-minute ask from Allison.

References / links (internal):
- Perf report (engineering): drive:shared_drives/engineering/serving-runtime/cascade-performance-report.pdf
- Incident JIRA: JIRA:CS-842
- Security checklist template: confluence:C-42891-account-health-cascade

Status: DRAFT — intentionally concise. Expect to iterate after sync with Eng and Finance.

-- End of draft --
